root_idea.summary: The root contains two distinct lexical fields: plant growth emerging around a base, and the side or bank of a valley or river.
root_idea.development: The growth branch extends to shoots, offshoots, and branches, while the spatial branch denotes a bank, shore, edge, or side. The lexical sources treat these as distinct branches rather than one unified direct meaning.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed as the normalized nominal citation form شَطْءٌ for the Quranic plant-growth usage.
Displayed as the normalized nominal citation form شَاطِئٌ for the Quranic bank-or-side usage.

senses.definition: A shoot, sprout, or offshoot emerging from around the base or stem of a plant.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expression أَخْرَجَ شَطْأَهُ, it denotes the young growth put forth by the plant.

senses.definition: The extremity, ears, or individual plants of a crop.
senses.usage_conditions: These are alternative lexical interpretations of شَطْأَهُ in the Quranic expression, alongside the sense of shoots or sprouts.

senses.definition: The bank, side, or shore of a valley, river, or sea; an edge or extremity.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrence, it denotes the side of a valley.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To walk along the bank or side of a river.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal use with the bank or side understood as the path of walking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cut lengthwise into slices or strips, especially a camel’s hump or a skin or hide.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object is a hump, skin, or hide cut into lengthwise pieces.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To subdue, overcome, overpower, or master.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive verbal use meaning to gain mastery over another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To approach sexually or have sexual intercourse.
To bind a saddle upon a she-camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the construction شَطَأَ النَّاقَةَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To burden heavily or overburden a camel with a load.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with بِالحِمْلِ in reference to imposing a heavy load.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have the strength or power to bear a load.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a person or a camel with reference to the ability to carry a load.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cast forth a child from the womb.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A construction describing a mother’s expelling or giving birth to a child.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a valley, to have its two sides flowing with water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction refers specifically to the valley’s two banks or sides.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To walk along one bank of a river or valley while another person walks along the opposite bank.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal or paired construction involving opposite sides.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of seed-produce, palm-trees, or trees, to put forth shoots, sprouts, or branches.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: With crops and palms it refers to putting forth shoots; with trees it can refer to branches emerging around the base or stem.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a man to have a son who reaches manhood and becomes like him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use describing a son’s maturation and resemblance to his father.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be weak in judgment and in one’s affairs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a person whose judgment or conduct is weak.
A nominal use for a fresh green branch of a palm.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A lengthwise slice or strip cut from a camel’s hump or from a skin or hide.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete noun for a piece produced by lengthwise cutting.

cautions: The two Quranic forms represent distinct lexical branches: شَطْءٌ concerns plant growth, while شَاطِئٌ concerns a bank or side.
The Quranic plant expression has several reported interpretations—shoots, extremity, ears, or plants—which are preserved as alternative lexical readings rather than treated as unrelated forms.
